title: "A 300-pound plus two-footed being:" Trump's Forest Service rejects 'Bigfoot' track claims following a wave of UFO file releases
excerpt: Donald Trump's Forest Service reportedly dropped secret case files on 'Bigfoot' after a wave of UFO file releases. The U.
content:
Rajarshi Deb

Updated Sat, November 21, 2026 at 8:56 AM UTC

Donald Trump's Forest Service reportedly dropped secret case files on 'Bigfoot' after a wave of UFO file releases. The U.S. Forest Service publicly disclosed Bigfoot records from its online archives on October 15 this year and created an excitement among people who are fascinated by the legendary creature. However, Forest Service wildlife biologist Rodney Johnson rejected claims that the tracks were genuine. He said,

"It is my opinion that the tracks observed at site A and site B along Low Creek were made by something other than a 300-pound-plus, two-footed being."

Bigfoot has long been part of American folklore and is often said to roam in forest areas across the United States but the only evidence ever presented was blurry photographs and eyewitness accounts.

Bigfoot admirers questioned the reason behind the release of the mysterious files. However, the enthusiasts remained hopeful that the Trump government might eventually make the secret documents public similar to the information it had already on UFOs.

Continue reading more about the story.

Donald Trump’s Forest Service quietly dropped 'Bigfoot' records

Trump's Forest Service had quietly released a secret government document related to Bigfoot. According to the released documents, investigators suspected footprints found in Washington's Mill Creek watershed on June 17, 1982, belongs to Bigfoot.

The department discovered 6 clearly visible footprints near Low Ridge that spread across roughly 25 feet of a muddy trail. As per their investigation, two of the prints measured about 15 inches in length.

The forest officials also found 18 footprints at a bog near the Low Creek Trail that extended roughly 40 feet toward dense vegetation. The team created two plaster casts at each of the locations where the footprints were discovered. However, they were not convinced that the footprints provided evidence of Sasquatch.

An experienced tracker named Rodney Johnson believed that the tracks had likely been created by a person rather than an unknown creature. Based on his observations, Rodney concluded that the tracks at Sites A and B along Low Creek were likely not made by a two-legged creature weighing more than 300 pounds.

Are Bigfoot and UFOs interlinked?

The interlinked concept between Bigfoot and UFOs became popular during the 1970s when public interest in both mysteries grew rapidly. According to Southern Styles Sweet Tees, reports and alleged evidence of Sasquatch increased across North America after people reported more UFO sightings. Researchers such as Stan Gordon investigated cases where unexplained lights and Sasquatch sightings appeared together.

Some reports also included electronic equipment failure, claims of telepathic communication, and Bigfoot seemingly appearing or disappearing suddenly. Locations such as Skinwalker Ranch, Mount Shasta, and Ocala Forest were frequently linked to both mysteries. Despite all these claims, no scientific evidence had confirmed a direct relationship between Bigfoot and UFOs.
